intro: Every card kind and zone from the stage-1 inventory, **today beside the prototype**, at 1600 and at 390. The proposed crops are screenshots of `proto/session-view.html` — **revised to grammar v2** after the critique — taken by the same instrument, with the same crop rule and the same names as today's, so the two columns cannot disagree about what was built.
howToRead: Each pair says the kind, the state, the principles (P1–P10) and breaks (B1–B13, grammar.md §1 and §7) that changed it, and one sentence on what changed. **Where the proposal reads worse than today, an amber note says so** — those are the most useful lines on the page. A kind the prototype did not convert, or that only a live document shows, says so instead of showing a fake. Click any image for the full-size crop. Timestamps differ between the columns because the fixture stamps *now*. At 390 both columns show the dev switch and, on the charter, the phone's task sheet over the card's foot: both are fixed to the window and the crop takes what the window shows.

6.1.title: 🪶 Title, settled, read by the Founder
6.1.by: P1 P3 P5 P7 P9 · B1 B2 B5 B11 B13
6.1.text: The head is the Rules paragraph the 🪶 tab hangs on, word for word, under a *Current rule* label; who chose it becomes one grey line of text instead of a pressed blue pill; the empty *Why are you changing this?* box and the 🗑️ with nothing to put back are gone until something is typed; the dark ✒️ ✏️ say *Give it a name first* in words.
6.1.resolved: v1: grammar §6.1 draws the head at the title's own size (`--h-title`); the prototype draws it at body size, so the head is the title's words but not the title as the page shows it. And the *The document is titled [A new title].* block restates the sentence form the head just dropped, so the card now names the title two ways. At 390 the head (title plus power line) and the fact line run to seven lines before the first choice. — **v2:** the settled 🪶 heads with the Rules paragraph word for word, *The document is titled “The Hollow Oak Club — House Charter”.*, at the paragraph's own size (the `--h-title` head is the birth's, and is built there); the power line leaves the head for the ✒️ 🛡️ cards (P3 v2), so the head and the new-title block now share one form rather than naming the title two ways; at 390 the head is one sentence and the fact line one more.

The dark ✓ says *Choose one of the three first*.
6.2.resolved: v1: the reader now learns that the second block is the proposal only after reading all of it and its rationale — *Proposed* sits by the radio at the block's foot, small and grey, where today it heads the block. — **v2:** *Proposed* is the block's first line, above its words, and *Current text* stands over the clause in the card's top inset — both read first, and the clause still opens level with its tab.

6.3.text: §6.3 names a live record; the fixture's `race-claims` stands in. *Decided · Tuesday, 29 September, 20:15* is the record's head label, first and in green, in the card's top inset — Q1522's *what it did first*, kept — so the clause still lands level with its ✔ tab (today 62–84 px lower); the participation line follows the winner's rationale; the rivals lose their boxes and are divided by hairlines, each labelled on its first line.

At 390 the one fact line wraps to four lines. — **v2:** every label is its block's first line, left, one drawing — *Rival · 58%*, *Previous text* — and the outcome is the head label, first (Q1522); the participation line alone is the fact, so at 390 it wraps to two lines, not four.

6.4.resolved: v1: the card is 23 px taller than today for one extra line of provenance, and that line sits between the current rule's radio and the proposal, where it reads as a caption for the proposal below it as easily as for the rule above. — **v2:** the fact line now stands between the rule and its *Prefer this* lane (§2.3 v2), so it reads as the rule's; the rule wears *Current rule* and the proposal *Proposed*. The card stays about as tall as v1 — the provenance line is the cost of saying who chose the rule.

zonesIntro: The prototype changed the cards, not the frame: the topbar, wallets, both rails, the drawers, edit mode and the stranger's door are loaded from today's files (LOG.md, stage 5). So the zone pairs below are few, and most say *unchanged*. The prototype's own *what is not converted* note (bottom-left) is hidden in every proposed crop, since today's page has no such furniture.

zones.title: The page, session fixture — the 📝 door, where Ed put it
zones.text: v1 moved the floating 📝 door inside the sheet to satisfy its own zone rule; v2 restores Ed's 2026-09-24 ruling — its centre on the sheet's right edge — and amends the rule instead: the floating layer is a sanctioned overlay that may cross a zone's edge but never covers a line of text (G4 v2). At 390 there is no door on either page.
zones.resolved: v1: inside the sheet the door now stands in the text's right margin, a few pixels from the ends of the lines at 1600, and it breaks Ed's 2026-09-24 ruling that it straddles the page edge (checks.md doubt 2, a break not yet numbered). — **v2:** the door straddles the page's edge again, and `zone-overlap` now measures the text it covers — none — rather than the zones it crosses. It still overlaps the left edge of the lowest queue entries' boxes by a few pixels, where no text stands: that is the ruling's known cost (diagnosis bug 6), now named rather than moved.

zones.title: The band (Rules), closed paragraphs — one change
zones.text: The closed band is the document's own text and the prototype leaves it as it is, with **one v2 change**: a Membership subsection's heading (*Invitees*, *Proposed for removal*) gains 4 px beneath it, so an open card's head label fits between the heading and the first row without touching either (G5's stated cost). The empty lists also say the STYLE-passed sentences (*Nobody has been invited yet.*) where they said *(no outstanding invitations)* (O9 (a)). Otherwise the paragraphs a card opens in place of are the same on both pages, which is what lets a card's head register with them.

zones.title: The desk and the two sheets — unchanged
zones.text: The seam between the Rules and the Text sheets.

zones.title: The closed page — unchanged when no card is open
zones.text: What changes on the closed page is inside the cards (above: no card offers an act but 🥂, and every card keeps what it recorded — P4 v2); the page itself is the same, and the topbar's ✏️ drip still counts on it, which v2 names but the prototype does not change.

zones.title: The phone: the task sheet raised and the contents drawer — unchanged
zones.text: MOBILE.md's first cut is kept; the prototype did not take O4 (a wider card at 390) — checks.md doubt 4.

zones.title: The founding, at arrival and after the save
zones.text: The birth's page before and after the save: the band's cards are closed here, so the pages match; the cards themselves are above under `birth`.

zones.title: Topbar and wallets
zones.notConverted: The topbar and the wallet sockets load from today's `session.js`/`wallets.js` family unchanged.
zones.text: Grammar §3.1 keeps the topbar as it is (nothing in it may move); the wallets are outside the card grammar.

zones.title: The two rails (contents and queue)
zones.notConverted: Both rails are today's. The diagnosis's rail finding (the contents rail's marks running past the drawer's glass at 390, bug 10) is not fixed in the prototype.

zones.title: Edit mode
zones.notConverted: Edit mode (the lifted column, the lane controls, the proposal row) is today's; B9 (one ✏️ in edit mode) is not built.

zones.title: The stranger's door
zones.notConverted: `door.js` is loaded from today's page; only the stranger's cards pass through the prototype's shell (above, `stranger`).

v2: **v2 (the revision pass).** The 39 amber notes stage 4 raised are each either **resolved** (a green box saying how, the v1 complaint quoted) or **kept** (still amber, with the reason). The v2 moves that answer most of them: **one label slot** (every block's label its first line, the head's in the card's top inset, drawn as today's eyebrow — grammar §2.3a); **a closed document keeps what it recorded** (P4 v2, B7 narrowed to settings rungs); **act and question cards carry their ask** as the head label (B3 withdrawn for O6 (b)); **a settings card heads with the rule's line alone**, the power line being the power cards' (P3 v2, Ed 2026-09-03); **a dark commit says why in words** (P5 v2); **the card ends at its content** and a long strip hangs on down the gutter (G6); and **Ed's 📝 door is back** where he ruled it (G4 v2).
